questions.question: List Shine on Wheels' start-up costs and calculate the total. Show how the total is financed.
questions.expected_answer: Pressure washer R6 500, water tanks R1 800, vacuum cleaner R2 200, trolley, buckets, towels and brushes R1 300, branding R1 200, permit and registration R500. Total R13 500. Financed by the owner's savings of R6 000 as capital plus a family loan of R7 500: 6 000 + 7 500 = 13 500.

questions.question: Shine on Wheels plans 120 washes a month at R120, with variable costs of R30 a wash and fixed costs of R5 300. Calculate the monthly profit and the break-even number of washes.
questions.expected_answer: Income 120 × 120 = R14 400. Variable costs 120 × 30 = R3 600. Profit 14 400 - 3 600 - 5 300 = R5 500. Each wash contributes 120 - 30 = R90. Break-even 5 300 ÷ 90 = 58.9, rounded up to 59 washes (59 × 90 = 5 310 covers 5 300; 58 × 90 = 5 220 does not).

questions.question: Name the four Ps and give one decision Shine on Wheels made for each. Name the business functions that the production and management plans relate to.
questions.expected_answer: Product: standard wash, inside-and-out wash and full valet. Price: R120 for a standard wash, below the competitor's R150. Place: the service goes to the customer, at home or at the office parks. Promotion: flyers, WhatsApp and Facebook posts, branded T-shirts and a referral offer. Production plan: production and purchasing functions. Management plan: general management and human resources.
